info.title: Huxley API
info.description: Huxley platform API. See https://docs.usehuxley.com for conventions.

get.summary: Lists audit events, newest first.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Only actions starting with this prefix, e.g. `auth.` or `org.created`.

post.summary: Emails the signed-in user a link to verify their address.
Verifies an address with the emailed link. No session needed.

Signs in with email and password. Sets the session cookie, or asks for a
second factor if the user has one.

200.description: Signed in (session cookie set), or a second factor is required

401.description: Wrong email or password, or the account is disabled or locked

429.description: Too many attempts from this address

post.summary:
Completes sign-in with a second factor. Send exactly one of `code` or
`recoveryCode`.

401.description: Wrong code, or the challenge expired or ran out of attempts

429.description: Too many attempts from this address

post.summary:
Options for answering an MFA challenge with a passkey. Finish with
`POST /api/v1/auth/login/mfa` and a `passkey` answer.

Signs in with a passkey alone. A passkey verifies the user on the device,
so no second factor is asked for.

401.description: The passkey could not be verified

post.summary: Options for passwordless sign-in with a passkey.
Signs out the current session and clears the cookie.

get.summary: The signed-in user.
Sign-in methods offered by this server.
The signed-in user's MFA setup.

post.summary: Replaces the recovery codes. The old ones stop working.

Starts setting up an authenticator app. Returns the secret to scan; the
app isn't required at sign-in until `/totp/confirm` succeeds.

Finishes authenticator setup with a code from the app. Returns recovery
codes (shown once) and signs out the user's other sessions.
Turns off the authenticator app and deletes recovery codes.

Completes single sign-on with the provider's `code` and `state`. Sets the
session cookie.

get.summary: Enabled sign-in options, for the sign-in page.

post.summary:
Starts single sign-on. The provider redirects back to
`{auth.public_url}/login/oidc/callback` with `code` and `state`.

get.summary: The signed-in user's passkeys.

post.summary: Finishes adding a passkey with the browser's answer.

422.description: Invalid answer, name, or expired request

post.summary: Starts adding a passkey (re-checks the password).

delete.summary:
Removes a passkey. Removing the last second factor also deletes the
recovery codes.

post.summary: Changes the signed-in user's password. Signs out all their other sessions.

204.description: Password changed; other sessions signed out

422.description: Current password wrong or new password too weak

post.summary:
Emails a password reset link if the address belongs to an account with a
password. Responds the same way whether or not it does.

202.description: If the account exists and can reset, a link is on its way

post.summary:
Sets a new password with a reset or invitation link. Signs out every
session; sign in again afterwards.

get.summary: The signed-in user's active sessions.

delete.summary: Revokes one of the signed-in user's sessions, e.g. a lost device.

404.description: No such session for this user

get.summary: Your API tokens. Needs a signed-in session (not a token).

post.summary:
Creates a personal access token that acts as you, narrowed to `scopes`.
It must expire within a year. Needs a signed-in session (not a token).

delete.summary: Revokes one of your API tokens.

get.summary: Every feature module and whether it's enabled and active.

put.summary:
Turns a feature module on or off for the instance. Data is kept when a
module is turned off.

409.description: Missing dependencies, or enabled modules depend on it

get.summary: Organizations the caller can see, ordered as a tree (parents before children).

post.summary: Creates a sub-organization.

409.description: Name already used by a sibling

post.summary: Archives an organization with no active sub-organizations.

Moves an organization and its subtree under a new parent. Requires
`org:move` on the organization and `org:create` on the new parent.

get.summary: Every permission Huxley checks.

post.summary: Grants a role to a user at an organization.

get.summary: Roles that can be assigned.
Who must have a second factor.

put.summary:
Requires (or stops requiring) a second factor for users who can reach an
organization. On the root organization, that's every user.

Requires (or stops requiring) a second factor for holders of a role.
Holders without one can only set one up until they do.

get.summary: Configured identity providers.

post.summary: Adds an identity provider.

get.summary: One provider with its role mappings.

put.summary: Replaces a provider's settings. Omit `clientSecret` to keep the stored one.

delete.summary:
Deletes a provider, the identities linked to it, and the roles its
mappings granted. Users are kept.

put.summary:
Replaces a provider's claim → role mappings. Applied at each user's next
sign-in. The Owner role can't be mapped.

get.summary: Service accounts: non-human identities for integrations and scripts.

post.summary:
Creates a service account. Grant it roles with `POST /role-assignments`,
then create tokens for it.

patch.summary: Renames, describes, disables, or re-enables a service account.

post.summary: Creates a token for a service account. It may be non-expiring.

get.summary: Teams. Anyone who can view users can view teams.
The teams a user belongs to.
A team with its members and role assignments.

delete.summary: Deletes a team and the roles it held. Members keep their own roles.

put.summary: Adds a user to a team (idempotent). They get the team's roles at once.

delete.summary: Removes a user from a team. They lose the team's roles at once.

get.summary: Lists users (people and service accounts; filter with `kind`).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page's `nextCursor`.

post.summary: Creates a local user. The new user has no roles until one is assigned.

patch.summary: Edits a user's name or status.

get.summary: A user's role assignments that the caller can see.

delete.summary:
Removes a user's second factors (authenticator app and recovery codes) and
signs them out everywhere, for when they've lost access to both. Only an
owner can reset an owner's MFA.

204.description: MFA removed; the user signs in with a password and can set it up again

get.summary: Liveness probe.
Readiness probe. Checks the database.

hint.description: The start of the token, to tell tokens apart.

teamId.description: Set for an assignment to a team.

userId.description: Set for an assignment to a user.

AuthMethodsView.description: Sign-in methods this server offers, for the sign-in page.

CeremonyView.description: The first half of a WebAuthn ceremony.

ceremony.description: Send back with the browser's answer.

code.description: A current six-digit code from the app.

inherit.description: Also apply to every sub-organization (default true).

teamId.description: Grant to this team; its members receive the role.

userId.description: Grant to this user. Send exactly one of `userId` or `teamId`.

expiresInDays.description: 1 to 366 for people. Omit (service accounts only) for no expiry.

scopes.description:
Permission keys the token may use, or `["*"]` for everything its
owner may do. Scopes only narrow the owner's roles.

invite.description:
Email the user an invitation to choose their own password instead.
Needs email to be configured.

password.description:
Initial password. If omitted (and not inviting), one is generated and
returned once.

generatedPassword.description: Present only when Huxley generated the password. Shown once.

tokenSecret.description: Send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Shown only now.

pointer.description: JSON Pointer to the invalid field, e.g. `/name`.

name.description: A label to tell passkeys apart, e.g. "Work laptop".

code.description: A six-digit code from the authenticator app.

recoveryCode.description: One of the user's recovery codes. Each works once.

oneOf.description: Signed in; the session cookie is set.

next.description: Where to go next (single sign-on remembers it across the redirect).

oneOf.description: The password was right; finish with `POST /api/v1/auth/login/mfa`.

challenge.description: Pass to `/login/mfa`. Valid for a few minutes and a few attempts.

LoginResponse.description: The result of a sign-in step.

activeModules.description: Feature modules that are enabled and released.

grantedPermissions.description:
Permissions granted at any organization. For deciding what to show;
the API enforces permissions on every request regardless.

isOwner.description: Holds the Owner role at the root organization.

mfaSetupRequired.description:
Policy requires a second factor and the user has none. Until they add
one, every API call except profile and MFA setup returns
`403 mfa-setup-required`.

MeView.description: The signed-in user plus permission hints for the UI.

MfaMethodView.description: Second-factor methods offered for a challenge.

MfaPolicy.description: The whole MFA policy at a glance.

everyone.description: Every user must have a second factor (set on the root organization).

orgs.description: Organizations whose users must have a second factor.

roleIds.description: Roles whose holders must have a second factor.

totpEnabled.description: An authenticator app is set up and required at sign-in.

MfaTrust.description: When an SSO sign-in counts as multi-factor for the MFA policy.

phase.description: Implementation-plan phase in which the module ships.

released.description: Whether this version of Huxley includes the module.

requires.description: Modules that must be enabled for this one to work.

active.description: Enabled and released: the module is running.

ModuleState.description: A module's state for the instance.

OrgKind.description:
`provider`: the owning company, an MSP brand, or a division. `client`: a
customer of a provider, or a site/sub-org of one.

depth.description: Depth in the tree; the root is 1.

version.description: Optimistic concurrency token. Send it back when updating.

PasskeyAnswer.description: The browser's answer to a passkey sign-in ceremony.

password.description: The user's current password, re-checked before the change.

isRoot.description: The root: the requirement covers every user.

Provider.description: A configured identity provider. The client secret is never returned.

ProviderButton.description: A sign-in button: the enabled providers, without configuration details.

redirectUri.description: Register this as the redirect URI at the provider.

ProviderDetail.description: A provider with its role mappings.

ProviderInput.description:
Settings for creating or replacing a provider. Optional fields fall back
to the preset's defaults.

allowedDomains.description: At least one. Only addresses in these domains may sign in.

clientSecret.description: Write-only. Omit on update to keep the stored secret.

key.description: Lowercase letters, digits, and dashes; appears in sign-in URLs.

name.description: Shown on the sign-in button, e.g. "Microsoft".

recoveryCodes.description: Shown only now. Each code signs in once if the authenticator is lost.
Present when this was the user's first second factor. Shown once.

requireMfa.description: Holders must have a second factor.

RoleMapping.description: A claim value → role at an org.

claimValue.description: The group id, app role, or other value of the provider's role claim.

current.description: True for the session making this request.

includeDependencies.description:
When enabling, also enable any modules it requires (default false:
respond 409 listing them instead).

changed.description: Modules whose setting changed, in the order they were applied.

next.description: A same-site path to return to afterwards.

state.description:
Bind to the browser (e.g. an `HttpOnly` cookie) and check it equals the
`state` the provider returns before calling `/callback`.

assignments.description: The team's role assignments that the caller can see.

TeamMember.description: A member, with enough about the user to display them.

otpauthUri.description: `otpauth://` URI to show as a QR code.

secret.description: Base32 secret, for entering into the app by hand.

version.description: The version you last read; the update fails with 409 if it changed.

status.description: `active` or `disabled`. Disabled accounts' tokens stop working.
`active` or `disabled`. Disabling signs the user out everywhere.

emailVerified.description: The user has proved they receive mail at `email`.

kind.description: `human` or `service` (a service account, which uses API tokens).

mfaEnabled.description: Has a second factor (authenticator app) set up.

tags.name: auth
tags.description: Sign-in, sessions, and the current user

tags.name: modules
tags.description: Feature modules that can be turned on or off
